chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran and Ali ibn Ibrahim, both together, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, who said:

I was with Abu al-Hasan Musa (عليه السلام) when a Christian man came to him while we were with him at al-'Urayd. The Christian said: “I have come to you from a distant land and a difficult journey. For thirty years I asked my Lord to guide me to the best of religions, and to the best and most knowledgeable of servants. Someone came to me in sleep and described to me a man in upper Damascus, so I went to him and spoke with him. He said: ‘I am the most knowledgeable among the people of my religion, but another is more knowledgeable than I.’ So I said: ‘Guide me to the one more knowledgeable than you, for travel is not too great for me, nor is the distance too far. I have read the whole Gospel, the Psalms of Dawud, four books of the Torah, and the outward of the Qur'an until I comprehended it all.’ The scholar said to me: ‘If you seek knowledge of Christianity, I am the most knowledgeable of Arabs and non-Arabs in it. If you seek knowledge of the Jews, then Bati ibn Shurahbil al-Samiri is the most knowledgeable of people in it today. But if you seek knowledge of Islam, and of the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the Book of Hud, and everything sent down upon any Prophet in your age and before it, and what has descended from heaven of report whether someone knew it or not—wherein is clarification of everything, healing for the worlds, comfort for the one who seeks repose in it, and insight for the one for whom Allah intends good and who inclines to the truth—then I will guide you to him. Go to him, even if walking on your feet; if you cannot, then crawling on your knees; if you cannot, then dragging yourself on your backside; if you cannot, then on your face.’ I said: ‘Rather, I am able to travel in body and wealth.’ He said: ‘Set out at once until you come to Yathrib.’ I said: ‘I do not know Yathrib.’ He said: ‘Go until you come to the city of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), who was sent among the Arabs, the Arab Hashimi Prophet. When you enter it, ask about Banu Ghanm ibn Malik ibn al-Najjar by the door of its mosque, and display the attire and adornment of Christianity, for its governor is harsh toward them and the caliph harsher still. Then ask about Banu 'Amr ibn Mabdhul at Baqi' al-Zubayr. Then ask about Musa ibn Ja'far—where his residence is and whether he is traveling or present. If he is traveling, then catch up to him, for his journey is nearer than the one you have already undertaken. Then inform him that the metropolitan of upper al-Ghutah, the Ghutah of Damascus, is the one who directed me to you, that he sends you many greetings, and says: I frequently beseech my Lord that He make my Islam at your hands.’”

He narrated this story while standing and leaning on his staff. Then he said: “If you permit me, my master, I will bow to you and sit.” He said: “I permit you to sit, but I do not permit you to bow.” So he sat, removed his hooded cloak, and said: “May I be your ransom, do you permit me to speak?” He said: “Yes, you came only for that.” The Christian said to him: “Return greetings to my companion—do you not return greetings?” Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام) said: “Upon your companion [be that] if Allah guides him. As for the greeting of peace, that is when he enters our religion.” The Christian said: “I ask you—may Allah set you right.” He said: “Ask.”

He said: “Inform me about the Book of Allah, the Exalted, which was sent down upon Muhammad and by which he spoke; then He described it as He described it, saying: ‘Ha Mim. By the clear Book. Indeed We sent it down in a blessed night; indeed We are warners. In it every wise matter is distinguished.’ What is its inner interpretation?”

He said: “As for Ha Mim, it is Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), and it is in the Book of Hud that was sent down to him, and it is abbreviated letters. As for the clear Book, it is Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (عليه السلام). As for the night, it is Fatimah (عليها السلام). And as for His saying, ‘In it every wise matter is distinguished,’ it means that much good comes forth from her: a wise man, and a wise man, and a wise man.” The man said: “Describe for me the first and the last of these men.” He said: “The descriptions resemble one another, but I shall describe to you the third of the people and what will come forth from his progeny. Indeed, it is with you in the books sent down to you—if you have not changed, altered, and disbelieved; and long have you done so.”

The Christian said to him: “I do not hide from you what I know, nor do I belie you, and you know what I say concerning the truth or falsehood of what I say. By Allah, Allah has given you from His فضل and allotted to you from His blessings what does not occur to those who imagine, what cannot be concealed by those who conceal, and concerning which even the denier cannot truly deny. So what I say to you about that is true as I have mentioned—it is as I have said.” Abu Ibrahim (عليه السلام) said to him: “I shall also hasten to tell you something that only a few among those who read the books know. Tell me: what is the name of Maryam's mother? On which day was Maryam breathed into, and at what hour of the day? On which day did Maryam give birth to 'Isa (عليه السلام), and at what hour of the day?” The Christian said: “I do not know.” Abu Ibrahim (عليه السلام) said: “As for Maryam's mother, her name was Martha, and in Arabic it is Wahibah. As for the day on which Maryam conceived, it was Friday at noon, and that is the day on which the Trustworthy Spirit descended. There is no 'Eid for the Muslims more deserving than it. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, magnified it, and Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) magnified it and ordered that it be made an 'Eid; thus it is Friday. As for the day on which Maryam gave birth, it was Tuesday, four and a half hours into the day. And the river by which Maryam gave birth to 'Isa (عليه السلام)—do you know it?” He said: “No.” He said: “It is the Euphrates, and by it are date-palms and grapevines, and nothing equals the Euphrates for vines and palms. As for the day on which she withheld her tongue, and Qaydus called his children and followers and they assisted him, and they brought out the family of 'Imran to look at Maryam, and they said to her what Allah related against you in His Book and against us in His Book—have you understood it?” He said: “Yes, and I read it today recently.” He said: “Then do not rise from your seat until Allah guides you.”

The Christian said: “What was my mother's name in Syriac and in Arabic?” He said: “Your mother's name in Syriac was 'Anqaliyah, and 'Unqurah was the name of your paternal grandmother. As for your mother's name in Arabic, it was Mayyah. As for your father's name, it was 'Abd al-Masih, which in Arabic is 'Abd Allah, and the Messiah has no slave.” He said: “You have spoken truly and excellently. Then what was my grandfather's name?” He said: “Your grandfather's name was Jibra'il, and that is 'Abd al-Rahman. I have named him so in this sitting of mine.” He said: “Was he then a Muslim?” Abu Ibrahim (عليه السلام) said: “Yes, and he was killed as a martyr. Troops entered upon him and killed him in his house secretly, and the troops were from the people of al-Sham.” He said: “What was my name before my kunyah?” He said: “Your name was 'Abd al-Salib.” He said: “Then what do you name me?” He said: “I name you 'Abd Allah.”

He said: “So I believe in Allah the Magnificent, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, singular and everlasting, not as the Christians describe Him, nor as the Jews describe Him, nor any kind among the kinds of shirk. And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He sent him with the truth, so by him He made it clear to its people, while the falsifiers became blind. He was the Messenger of Allah to all people, to the red and the black; all share equally in that. So whoever saw, saw; whoever was guided, was guided; and the falsifiers were blinded, and what they used to call upon was lost from them. And I bear witness that his wali spoke with his wisdom, and that those before him among the Prophets spoke with perfect wisdom, supported one another in obedience to Allah, separated from falsehood and its people, from impurity and its people, abandoned the path of misguidance, and Allah aided them through obedience to Him and protected them from disobedience. Thus they are Allah's awliya' and supporters of the religion, urging to good and commanding it. I believe in the young among them and the old, those I have mentioned and those I have not mentioned, and I believe in Allah, Blessed and Exalted, Lord of the worlds.”

Then he cut his belt and cut off a gold cross that had been on his neck. Then he said: “Command me where to place my charity.” He said: “Here is a brother of yours who had been upon a religion like yours. He is a man from your people, from Qays ibn Tha'labah, and he is in blessing like your blessing. So console one another and live near one another, and I will not neglect to convey to you both your due right in Islam.” He said: “By Allah, may Allah set you right, I am wealthy. I have left three hundred breeding horses, male and female, and left one thousand camels, so your right therein is fuller than my own right.” He said to him: “You are the mawla of Allah and His Messenger, and in the limit of your lineage you remain upon your state.” The narrator said: “His Islam became excellent. He married a woman from Banu Fihr, and Abu Ibrahim (عليه السلام) gave her fifty dinars as her dower from the charity of Ali ibn Abi Talib (عليه السلام), provided him with a servant, settled him, and he remained until Abu Ibrahim (عليه السلام) was taken out. Then he died twenty-eight nights after his departure.”

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَىٰ: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (عليه السلام), the central figure addressed in the narration.
key_terms.الشِّرْكِ: Association of partners with Allah, explicitly rejected in the convert's confession of faith.
key_terms.اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُبَارَكَةُ: Interpreted here in the inner sense as Fatimah (عليها السلام).
key_terms.الْكِتَابُ الْمُبِينُ: In this hadith's inner explanation, a title referring to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (عليه السلام).
key_terms.صَدَقَتِي: The convert's charitable wealth, which he asks the Imam to direct appropriately.
key_terms.فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ: Indicates, in the hadith's batini interpretation, the emergence of wise figures from her line.
key_terms.مُنَاجَاةَ رَبِّي: Intimate supplication to Allah, mentioned by the bishop who prayed to accept Islam through the Imam.
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: The divinely appointed successor of the Prophet, affirmed in the convert's testimony.

ai.seo_question: How did a Christian scholar recognize Imam Musa al-Kazim (عليه السلام) and what inner meaning did he give to Qur'an 44:1-4?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the journey of a Christian seeker who is guided to Imam Musa al-Kazim (عليه السلام), recognizes his divinely granted knowledge, and embraces Islam. It also includes a batini explanation of Qur'an 44:1-4, linking its symbols to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (عليه السلام), Sayyidah Fatimah (عليها السلام), and the blessed progeny that emerge from her.
